- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from 10-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment < -0.2.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices in early 30-day window when sentiment is volatile; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment swings >0.3 in 5-day window.
- If model forecast > true outcome by >3% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
